title: What the parties say on the West Bank
question: Should Israel annex West Bank land?

stances.label: Annex Area C or chosen areas

note: Most rows are from the parties' answers to a Ynet questionnaire (Sept 30, 2026). Likud does not take part in questionnaires; its row is its statement on the October 2025 bills. Noam's row is from 2025; no 2026 answer was found. 'Judea and Samaria' appears here as the parties wrote it. Checked October 2026. Shas and UTJ answered without taking a position on annexation.

rows.text: On the October 2025 annexation bills, on which Netanyahu told its MKs to abstain: "Another provocation by the opposition aimed at damaging our relations with the United States… True sovereignty will be achieved not through a showy law for the record, but through proper work on the ground."
Says it "eliminated the idea of a Palestinian state"; supports "applying full Israeli sovereignty over Judea and Samaria."

"Apply full Israeli sovereignty, dismantle the Palestinian Authority of its assets and weapons" and "encourage voluntary migration from Judea and Samaria and Gaza"; new communities in all parts of the territory; of outposts: "We will regularize them."
Amcha Yisrael: "A Palestinian state will never be established alongside us"; "apply sovereignty in Judea and Samaria."
Avi Maoz sponsored the 2025 sovereignty bill that passed 25–24: "We are correcting a historical wrong that is long overdue."

Opposes the establishment of a Palestinian state; says that, as one of the "founders of the right-wing bloc," it has supported initiatives promoted by Religious Zionism and Otzma Yehudit; per Ynet, does not make West Bank settlement policy a central campaign issue.
Gave no unified position. Ynet reports that Agudat Yisrael generally leans further right, Degel HaTorah takes a more moderate position, and neither makes the issue central to its campaign.

A Palestinian state "is not on the agenda"; "strengthening the settlement blocs and establishing new communities legally"; "Israel has no interest in assuming responsibility for the civilian lives of some 2 million Palestinians."
"Oppose a Palestinian state and the transfer of territory"; "Area C is viewed as a future sovereign part of the State of Israel."
"We support applying Israeli sovereignty to Area C"; "advancing construction in the E1 area"; "Thirty-three years after the Oslo Accords, it is clear that the experiment failed."
"The party supports sovereignty through actions, not words"; "The strategy is to seize commanding terrain and agricultural land."
"Strengthening settlement in Judea and Samaria, with an emphasis on the Jordan Valley…"; per Ynet, a framework similar to the Trump plan that would not require evacuating settlements.
"We must strive for separation as part of a regional move" with the United States; "We will evacuate illegal outposts that create points of friction."
Per Ynet, supports a negotiated two-state solution, with a Palestinian state alongside Israel; opposes extending Israeli sovereignty.
"All settlements… must be evacuated immediately and without delay"; "The occupation is the root of all evil"; asked that the question say "the occupied West Bank."
